faqs.question: What do I actually send him — a link, or a file?
faqs.answer: A link. The page lives on the web and he opens it in a browser, so there is nothing to download, install or sign up for, and nothing arrives in his gallery unless he screenshots it.

faqs.question: Can I stop him forwarding the gift link to someone else?
faqs.answer: Not really. A password stops whoever he forwards it to from seeing the page, but it cannot stop him passing the URL on, and 40.6% of SubhSandesh creators set one before sharing for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: He opened it on his office laptop and half of it did not load. Why?
faqs.answer: Managed work devices often block outside domains, fonts or media, and data-saving modes can make a browser request lighter versions of images and video. Ask him to reopen it on his own phone on normal data.

faqs.question: He has not opened it yet. Should I resend the link or wait?
faqs.answer: Wait a few hours before resending. Pages on SubhSandesh average 11.5 opens each across 49,968 recorded views, so the first open is rarely the last, and a second message tends to explain the surprise before he sees it.

faqs.question: Can I make the link unlock exactly at midnight?
faqs.answer: I cannot confirm a scheduled-unlock feature on SubhSandesh, so do not plan around one. The reliable method is to finish the page early and send the message at the hour you want.

faqs.question: What if he loses the message and cannot find the link again?
faqs.answer: Send it once more from your own chat history, since the URL does not change when you edit the page. It is worth saving the address somewhere outside the chat the day you build it.

faqs.question: Is a QR code better than a link if he is in another city?
faqs.answer: No. A QR code only helps when you can physically hand over paper; at a distance it adds a scan step and the same URL is doing the work anyway.

faqs.question: How long should the password be if he is typing it on a phone?
faqs.answer: Short. 49.0% of opens happen on a phone, usually one-handed, so a long passphrase is a barrier rather than a security gain — and it should not be a date the two of you would argue about.

faqs.question: Is a virtual gift link for a boyfriend free to make?
faqs.answer: SubhSandesh's internal facts file carries no confirmed pricing, so this post will not state one. Check the current terms on the template gallery before you plan around a free build.

faqs.question: Will he be able to tell I made it myself rather than bought it?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and that is the point. The details that read as handmade are the specific ones — a date, an inside joke, a photo nobody else has — not the polish of the template.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Virtual Gift Link for Boyfriend: What the Link Does Next

A virtual gift link for a boyfriend is a private URL pointing at a page you built for him. He taps it, the page opens in whatever browser his phone hands it to, and nothing is downloaded, delivered or shipped.

The link is the packaging, and it behaves in ways a wrapped box does not. It can be previewed before he opens it, forwarded after he does, edited while he is still looking at it, and quietly stop working a year from now.

Two numbers from SubhSandesh's own database explain why that matters. 49.0% of opens happen on a phone (24,493 of 49,968 recorded views, measured 2026-09-15), and the average page is opened 11.5 times — this is not a thing he looks at once. Everything below is about the link itself: the preview card, editing after sending, passwords, and what survives a year.

## What a virtual gift link for a boyfriend actually is

It is one unlisted web address that loads a page of your photos, messages or jokes about him. Anyone holding that address can open it, and nobody without it can find it, because it is not listed anywhere a search engine crawls.

That is the whole access model. SubhSandesh has recorded 4,357 personalised pages across 16 page types since 2026-03-12, and 94.1% of started pages are published and shared (4,098 of 4,357, measured 2026-09-15) — the abandonment happens before the link exists, not after.

## What his phone shows before he taps the link

When you paste the URL into a chat, the messaging app goes and fetches the page itself to build the preview card. Slack's developer documentation describes this plainly for its own default behaviour: [when a link is spotted, Slack crawls it and provides a preview](https://api.slack.com/reference/messaging/link-unfurling). Most chat apps do some version of the same thing.

That has one consequence people discover too late. Whatever title and image your page hands an unauthenticated crawler is what appears in his chat before he has decided to tap — and it is also what anyone glancing at his lock screen reads. Check it rather than assume it.

There is a second device variable. If he has a data-saving mode on, his browser can send a `Save-Data: on` request header, and the [W3C Community Group Save Data specification](https://wicg.github.io/savedata/) says an origin may then deliver "smaller image and video resources, alternate markup, and so on". A page you built on office Wi-Fi is not guaranteed to look identical on his 4G.

This is where a deliberately official-looking format has an advantage. The SubhSandesh [mock traffic challan page](https://subhsandesh.in/challan) — a fake e-challan for things he actually did, which he can pay or contest — is funnier the more bureaucratic its preview card looks, so the card giving the game away is the point rather than the problem.

## Can you edit the page, or take it back, after you send it?

No. You cannot unsend a URL — you can only change what it points to, and he may already be looking at it when you do.

This is not a hypothetical risk on this platform. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.2 hours, sampled on the "I love you" page (n=1,125, measured 2026-09-15), which means a great many pages are still being worked on hours after they were first created. Since 94.1% of started pages get published, plenty of those edits are happening to live addresses.

The rule is dull and correct: finish it, then send it. If you must send early, tell him it is not done, because a half-built page read as a finished one is worse than a wait.

Deletion cuts both ways. If you can delete the page he loses it too, and at 11.5 average opens he is likelier to come back than you think. The [prepaid relationship recharge](https://subhsandesh.in/recharge) — he picks a plan, pays on a sheet that mimics the real thing, gets a receipt — leaves him something screenshot-shaped that survives independently of the link.

## Three checks to run before you paste it into his chat

Three checks, in order, close the failure modes that actually happen — the preview, the phone, and the 40.6% decision.

### 1. Send the link to yourself first

Open the chat you are going to use, paste the URL, and look at the card the app builds. You are checking the title, description and image — the properties the Open Graph protocol standardised and that chat apps read.

If the card names the surprise, the surprise is over before he taps.

### 2. Open it once on a phone, not on the laptop you built it on

49.0% of all opens on SubhSandesh are on a phone (24,493 of 49,968 views), so the phone rendering is the real one. Long captions, wide tables and anything that needs a hover are the usual casualties.

### 3. Set the password before you send, not after

40.6% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,767 of 4,357, measured 2026-09-15). Adding one afterwards does not help if the link has already been forwarded, because the forwarding already happened.

Keep it short. He is typing it one-handed on a phone.

## What you can take back, and what you cannot

Different things you can send him have very different recall and survival properties. This table compares them on the two questions that matter after the moment has passed.

| What you sent | Can you change it afterwards | Still there in a year | SubhSandesh measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| A link to a page you control | Yes — edit the page, the URL stays | Only while the page is hosted | Median 6.2h first save to last edit (n=1,125) |
| A screenshot he took of the page | No | Yes, it sits in his gallery | 49.0% of opens are on a phone |
| The link after he forwards it | No, and you cannot see who holds it | Same lifespan as the page | 40.6% set a password before sharing |
| A printed QR code on a card | No | Only if the link behind it survives | 11.5 average opens per page |

The pattern is that everything you keep control of is also everything that can disappear, and everything permanent is a copy you no longer control.

## Why putting a password on his page is a relationship question

The 40.6% figure above is usually read as a security setting. It is at least as much a relational one, because handing a partner a password is a documented relationship behaviour rather than a neutral act.

In a 2024 study of 948 US adults currently or recently in romantic relationships, [Vendemia and Bevan found that relationship satisfaction, relationship length and social networking site jealousy each predicted password sharing](https://digitalcommons.chapman.edu/comm_articles/145/), and that distrust-and-suspicion reasons for sharing were negatively related to satisfaction. Only the abstract was readable, so that is the whole of what can be claimed from it.

A password also does not solve forwarding. A 2017 First Monday study built on 34 semi-structured interviews found that [trust, confidentiality and consent are the fundamental conditions for photo-sharing in close relationships](https://firstmonday.org/ojs/index.php/fm/article/view/7860), while participants simultaneously treated trust and confidentiality as fragile, and usually held the person who made the image responsible for unintended re-sharing.

One disclosure, because it changes how you should read every number here: the SubhSandesh database records which template was opened, not who received it. A count against the "I love you" page does not prove the recipient was a boyfriend.

## Whether the link still exists a year from now

Links decay, and the best-measured version of this comes from legal citation. In the Harvard Law Review Forum, [Zittrain, Albert and Lessig reported that of 555 URLs cited in US Supreme Court opinions, 136 (24.5%) returned a 404](https://harvardlawreview.org/forum/vol-127/perma-scoping-and-addressing-the-problem-of-link-and-reference-rot-in-legal-citations/), and of the 353 that still returned HTTP 200, only 277 — 78.5% — actually showed the material originally cited. Their overall reference-rot figure for those citations was about 50%.

A dead address is not a neutral outcome either. At the ACM Web Conference 2024, Saric and colleagues [found active links on the web pointing to more than 572,000 .com domains that had never been registered](https://eprints.qut.edu.au/245862/), registered 51 of them, and saw 88% of those "phantom domains" exceed a control domain's traffic, with up to ten times more visits, at under $20 per domain.

The lesson for a gift is small and specific. Keep the contents outside the page — download the photos, screenshot the receipt — so the memory does not depend on one URL staying alive. A format built to be reopened, like the [long-distance train ticket page](https://subhsandesh.in/train-ticket) where he checks the PNR, watches the waitlist clear and reads the running status of the relationship, is worth more the longer it survives.

## When a virtual gift link is the wrong thing to send him

If he is in the same room, give him the object. A link asks him to take his phone out in front of you, which is the opposite of what you wanted.

It is also a poor fit for a locked-down work phone, and for anyone who genuinely never reopens links — 11.5 opens per page is an average, and averages hide the people who look once. For the gift's register rather than the link's mechanics, [our post on picking a virtual gift for a bf](https://subhsandesh.in/blog/virtual-gift-for-bf) argues for joke formats over sincere ones, and [what goes on a shareable gift link for couples](https://subhsandesh.in/blog/shareable-gift-link-for-couples) covers the page contents.

On cost: SubhSandesh's internal facts file carries no confirmed pricing, so this post will not quote a figure it cannot source. Check the current terms on the [SubhSandesh template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

## Sources

- Zittrain, Albert & Lessig, "Perma: Scoping and Addressing the Problem of Link and Reference Rot in Legal Citations", Harvard Law Review Forum vol. 127, March 2014.
- Saric, Savins, Ramachandran, Jurdak & Nepal, "Hyperlink Hijacking: Exploiting Erroneous URL Links to Phantom Domains", ACM Web Conference 2024, 8 May 2024.
- Vendemia & Bevan, "Why Do People Share Social Networking Site Passwords with Their Romantic Partners?", Communication Research Reports, 24 October 2024 — abstract only.
- Venema & Lobinger, "'And somehow it ends up on the Internet.' Agency, trust and risks in photo-sharing among friends and romantic partners", First Monday 22(7), 3 July 2017.
- Slack developer documentation, "Unfurling links in messages".
- W3C Community Group, "Save Data API" specification.
